name: Evaluation and Benchmarking of LLM Agents: A Survey (Mohammadi et al.; sometimes mislabeled 'Yehudai et al.')
venue: Peer-reviewed: KDD '25 (Proceedings of the 31st ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining), Aug 3-7 2025, Toronto, ON, Canada, DOI 10.1145/3711896.3736570 (survey/lecture-style paper). Preprint: arXiv:2507.21504 [cs.LG, cs.AI], submitted 29 Jul 2025 (v1), CC BY 4.0.
authors_affiliation: Mahmoud Mohammadi, Yipeng Li, Jane Lo, Wendy Yip -- all SAP Labs (Bellevue, WA and Palo Alto, CA, USA). NOTE: the task brief attributed this to 'Yehudai et al.'; that is a different agent-evaluation survey (Yehudai et al., 'Survey on Evaluation of LLM-based Agents', arXiv:2503.16416). The paper at the given URL (2507.21504) is authored by Mohammadi, Li, Lo, Yip (SAP Labs).
code_url: N/A (survey; no accompanying code/method release found; the paper points to surveyed tools/benchmarks but ships no runnable implementation of its own).
maintained_repo_url: N/A (no continuously-maintained authors' GitHub paper-list/leaderboard located for this survey).
task_domain: Survey / taxonomy of LLM-agent EVALUATION. Cross-domain: covers tool-use, planning/reasoning, memory/context-retention, multi-agent collaboration, web/app agents, software-engineering, scientific, healthcare and finance agents, plus reliability and safety/alignment evaluation; not restricted to one task domain.
problem_setting: This is a literature survey (no method, no experiments of its own). It addresses how to evaluate LLM-based agents and proposes a two-dimensional taxonomy: (1) Evaluation Objectives = WHAT to evaluate (Agent Behavior: task completion, output quality, latency&cost; Agent Capabilities: tool use, planning&reasoning, memory&context retention, multi-agent collaboration; Reliability: consistency, robustness; Safety&Alignment: fairness, harm/toxicity/bias, compliance&privacy) and (2) Evaluation Process = HOW to evaluate (Interaction Mode: static&offline vs dynamic&online; Evaluation Data: synthetic/real-world datasets, domain benchmarks; Metrics Computation Methods: code-based, LLM-as-a-Judge / Agent-as-a-Judge, human-in-the-loop; Evaluation Tooling: instrumentation frameworks and leaderboards; Evaluation Contexts: simulation to open-world web/API). It also raises enterprise-specific challenges (role-based data access, reliability guarantees, dynamic/long-horizon interactions, compliance) and future directions (holistic, more realistic, scalable evaluation). It surveys both static/offline and interactive/online and both single- and multi-agent settings, but defines no controlled experimental protocol, supervision, or benchmark of its own.
what_is_retrieved: N/A as an artifact (the survey itself retrieves nothing). As a surveyed topic it discusses agents that retrieve TOOLS from large tool repositories (tool retrieval over candidate toolsets) and that retain/recall MEMORY/context across long dialogues; tool descriptions, prior conversation turns, and intermediate working-memory results are the surveyed retrieved/recalled content.
retrieval_grounding: N/A for the survey (no grounding corpus of its own). The surveyed evaluation landscape spans BOTH retrieval over STATIC external tool/API repositories (tool retrieval, function-calling over candidate sets) and GROWING/episodic agent MEMORY (context retention over 40+ to 600+ turn dialogues; working memory of intermediate results), i.e. it reviews both static-corpus retrieval and growing-memory settings.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: N/A (survey, no retrieval objective of its own). It NOTES the relevant evaluation distinction: tool retrieval is scored with top-k rank accuracy, MRR and NDCG (ranking objective), while planning/multi-tool tasks are scored against a complete reference tool SET/sequence via Node F1, Edge F1 and Normalized Edit Distance (completeness-of-the-needed-set framing). The survey itself prescribes no single objective.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (the survey is not a case-based reasoning system; it implements no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain cycle).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The survey does not frame agent evaluation as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is organized around the WHAT/HOW (objectives/process) evaluation taxonomy.
retrieval_unit: N/A (survey defines no retrieval unit of its own). Surveyed units include: tool-API (single function/tool retrieved from a repository for function calling) and memory entries (prior dialogue turns, intermediate working-memory results) recalled during long-horizon interaction.
index_source: N/A for the survey (it builds no index). Surveyed tool retrieval is over static external tool/API repositories (e.g., large API sets in ToolBench/API-Bank/TaskBench); surveyed memory is a growing/online store the agent accumulates during multi-turn interaction.
index_structure_topology: N/A (survey has no index of its own). It notes that some surveyed planning/tool benchmarks adopt GRAPH-based representations of tools (dependency/ordering graphs, scored with Node F1 / Edge F1 / Normalized Edit Distance), alongside flat candidate tool lists -- i.e. it reviews both flat and graph-structured tool organizations rather than prescribing one.
retriever_type: N/A (survey; no retriever implemented). It references retrieval of the correct tool from a large toolset based on a natural-language task description and ranking-based evaluation (rank accuracy@k, MRR, NDCG), implying dense/similarity tool retrievers in surveyed systems, but contributes no retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: N/A (survey; trains no retriever). It catalogs how tool-retrieval QUALITY is measured (Retrieval Accuracy, MRR, NDCG) rather than how a retriever is trained.
query_construction: N/A (survey). For surveyed tool retrieval the query is the natural-language task/intent description matched against tool descriptions; for surveyed memory recall the current request/turn acts as the query against stored conversation history. The survey proposes no query-construction method.
query_granularity: N/A (survey). Surveyed agents query at the step/decision level (per tool-call decision; per-turn memory recall) and at the task level (multi-tool plan over a task); the survey reviews both rather than fixing one.
when_to_retrieve: N/A (survey). It frames the relevant evaluation question 'can the agent correctly determine WHETHER tool invocation is necessary' (Invocation Accuracy) and contrasts plan-ahead vs interleaved ReAct-style retrieve/act-during-execution paradigms; it standardizes no single timing.
retrieval_trigger_signal: N/A (survey defines no trigger). Surveyed agent-initiated tool invocation is decided by the model itself (native function-calling: the model autonomously decides whether to invoke a function), and memory recall is agent-initiated per request; evaluation of this decision is captured by Invocation Accuracy.
reranking: N/A (survey; no reranking stage of its own). It mentions ranking-based tool-retrieval evaluation (rank accuracy@k, MRR, NDCG) as a measurement, not a reranking pipeline it contributes.
retrieved_context_refinement: N/A (survey). It discusses memory operations such as appropriate forgetting of irrelevant details and tracking intermediate (working-memory) results in surveyed agents, but proposes no refinement pipeline of its own.
tool_document_engineering: N/A as a contribution. It notes (surveyed) that, when the candidate toolset is extensive, an agent must retrieve the correct tool from a repository based on a natural-language task description, and that tool descriptions/parameter schemas are matched -- but it proposes no tool-document-engineering technique.
index_content_separation: N/A (survey; no lightweight-index-then-content mechanism of its own).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A as a contribution. It surveys native function-calling/function invocation and large API repositories (ToolBench/API-Bank/TaskBench, Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard) and dynamic/online agent-environment interaction (web browsers, APIs), but does not center a live-synchronized tool index or a specific protocol (e.g., MCP) of its own.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A as a contribution. It NOTES that tool order and inter-tool dependency matter and that some surveyed benchmarks use graph-based tool representations with Node F1 (selection) and Edge F1 / Normalized Edit Distance (sequence/structure) to capture dependencies -- but contributes no dependency-aware retriever itself.
how_retrieved_used: N/A as a method. The survey describes how agents USE retrieved/recalled content (tools invoked for actions/grounding; memory recalled to maintain consistency across long-horizon tasks; ReAct-style interleaving of reasoning and tool use), and how EVALUATION consumes agent outputs (code-based checks, LLM-as-a-Judge / Agent-as-a-Judge, human-in-the-loop). It implements nothing.
planning_integration: N/A as a method. It reviews planning/reasoning evaluation: static plan comparison against a reference tool set/sequence (T-Eval set-based planning; graph-based Node F1 / Edge F1 / Normalized Edit Distance per TaskBench), interleaved plan-and-execute (ReAct) with step-wise reasoning metrics (T-Eval reasoning metric; AgentBoard Progress Rate), program-style multi-step plans scored with code-generation/program-similarity metrics (ScienceAgentBench), and Step Success Rate. It proposes no single integration.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: N/A (survey). It contrasts plan-ahead (static full plan vs reference) with per-step interleaved reasoning+tool-use (ReAct), and notes step-level reasoning metrics (T-Eval next-tool-call alignment per step; AgentBoard Progress Rate per trajectory step) -- reviewing per-step vs per-trajectory evaluation rather than committing to one.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not a CBR method; no retrieved-case adaptation of its own).
retrieved_item_representation: N/A (survey). Surveyed retrieved/recalled content is represented as tool/API descriptions and call signatures (with parameter schemas) and as natural-language conversation memory / intermediate results; the survey injects nothing itself.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: N/A (survey). Surveyed units range from raw conversation turns (episodic memory) to single tool/API calls and to multi-step plans/programs; the survey reviews this spectrum rather than fixing an abstraction level.
noise_robustness_mechanism: N/A as a contribution. Robustness is a first-class EVALUATION TARGET in the taxonomy (Reliability -> Robustness; Safety -> resilience to prompt-injection via AgentDojo; harmful-behavior testing via AgentHarm), so the survey reviews how robustness is MEASURED, but contributes no robustness mechanism of its own.
memory_type: N/A as an artifact. As a surveyed evaluation target, Memory and Context Retention is an explicit capability category (Section 3.2.3): episodic conversation memory (Memory Span / Memory Forms per Guan et al. 2024), long-dialogue context retention (40+ to 600+ turns), and working memory for tool-using agents (tracking intermediate results) plus forgetting strategies. The survey itself has no memory.
write_back: N/A as a method. Surveyed long-running agents accumulate/retain memory across turns and track intermediate results, but the survey stores nothing itself (boolean: False for the artifact).
online_growth: N/A as a method. Surveyed agent memory grows online during multi-turn/long-horizon interaction; the survey itself has no growing store.
write_back_trigger: N/A (survey; no write-back trigger of its own). Surveyed memory accumulation is per-turn/per-interaction during deployment; the survey standardizes no trigger.
failure_experience_usage: N/A (survey). It evaluates robustness/error handling (whether agents behave robustly when the system encounters errors) and execution-based outcomes (Gorilla-style running of tool calls to catch failures), implying use of failure signals in surveyed evaluation, but contributes no failure-experience storage scheme.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (survey). It notes forgetting strategies (appropriately forgetting irrelevant details) and consistency tracking across turns as surveyed memory dynamics, but proposes no single update/evolution policy.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: N/A (survey). It does not center retrieval/case-selection as a learned RL policy; surveyed tool retrieval is described via ranking metrics (rank@k/MRR/NDCG) and native function-calling decisions, not a trained retrieval policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A as a method. Multi-Agent Collaboration is an explicit surveyed evaluation CAPABILITY (Section 3.2.4), and Agent-as-a-Judge (multiple AI agents interacting to refine assessment) is surveyed as a metric-computation method; the survey reviews multi-agent settings but implements no cross-agent memory sharing itself.
benchmarks: N/A (survey; runs no experiments of its own). It CATALOGS many agent-evaluation benchmarks/datasets/leaderboards, including: Tool use / function-calling: TaskBench (Shen et al. 2024), ToolBench (Huang et al. 2024b), API-Bank (Li et al. 2023), T-Eval (Chen et al. 2024b), Gorilla/Gorilla-APIBench (Patil et al. 2023), Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard (BFCL, Yan et al. 2024). Memory/context retention: LongEval (Krishna et al. 2023), SocialBench (Chen et al. 2024a), LoCoMo (Maharana et al. 2024, 600+ turns), Optimus-1 (Li et al. 2024d, NeurIPS 2024). Planning/reasoning & science: ScienceAgentBench (Chen et al. 2025), AAAR-1.0 (Lou et al. 2025), AgentBoard (Ma et al. 2024), FlowBench (Xiao et al. 2024). Web/app interactive: AssistantBench (Yoran et al. 2024), AppWorld (Trivedi et al. 2024), WebArena (Zhou et al. 2023). Safety/robustness: AgentHarm (Andriushchenko et al. 2025), AgentDojo (Debenedetti et al. 2024). Leaderboards: BFCL, Holistic Agent Leaderboard (Stroebl et al. 2025).
benchmark_family: N/A (survey reports no benchmark family results of its own). Surveyed families: tool/function-calling (TaskBench, ToolBench, API-Bank, T-Eval, BFCL, Gorilla), memory (LongEval, SocialBench, LoCoMo, Optimus-1), planning/science (ScienceAgentBench, AAAR-1.0, AgentBoard, FlowBench), web/app interactive (WebArena, AppWorld, AssistantBench), and safety/robustness (AgentHarm, AgentDojo).
baselines: N/A (survey; no method comparison or baselines of its own).
key_metrics: N/A (survey reports no metrics of its own). It CATALOGS agent-evaluation metrics it surveys: Task Success Rate; Invocation Accuracy; Tool Selection Accuracy; Retrieval Accuracy (rank accuracy@k), MRR, NDCG; parameter name F1; AST correctness and execution-based correctness (Gorilla); Node F1 / Edge F1 / Normalized Edit Distance (graph-structured plans, TaskBench); T-Eval reasoning metric; AgentBoard Progress Rate; Step Success Rate; Win Rate; factual recall accuracy and consistency score (memory); plus latency & cost, fairness/toxicity/bias, and robustness measures.
headline_result: N/A (survey; no headline number). Its central contribution is the two-dimensional WHAT/HOW taxonomy (Evaluation Objectives x Evaluation Process) for LLM-agent evaluation, plus the enterprise-challenge framing (role-based access, reliability guarantees, long-horizon interactions, compliance) and future directions (holistic, realistic, scalable evaluation).
ablations: N/A (survey; conducts no experiments and therefore reports no ablations).
evaluation_decoupling: N/A (the survey reports no metrics of its own). It DOES analytically separate intrinsic capability/retrieval metrics (e.g., tool Retrieval Accuracy, MRR, NDCG, Node/Edge F1, parameter F1, Progress Rate, Step Success Rate) from end-to-end Task Completion / Task Success Rate within its Metrics discussion, i.e. it surveys both intrinsic and end-to-end metrics as distinct layers.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Surveyed (a core organizing theme): the taxonomy explicitly distinguishes outcome-oriented Agent Behavior (task completion, output quality) from process-oriented Agent Capabilities (tool use, planning/reasoning, memory, multi-agent), and surveys step-wise/process metrics (T-Eval reasoning metric, AgentBoard Progress Rate, Step Success Rate, trajectory comparison) alongside final-outcome metrics. The survey itself scores nothing.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Surveyed: Latency & Cost is an explicit Agent-Behavior evaluation sub-category (Section 3.1.3), and scalability/cost of evaluation (LLM-as-a-Judge scalability vs human-in-the-loop reliability; Evaluation-driven Development tooling for scalable continuous evaluation) is discussed throughout. The survey reports no cost/efficiency numbers of its own.
context_budget_and_selection_count: N/A (survey; no token budget or k of its own). Long-context/long-horizon retention (40+ to 600+ turn dialogues) and context-window limits are surveyed as evaluation challenges, but no fixed-k or token budget is prescribed.
survey_scope_and_axes: Primary organizing axes: a TWO-DIMENSIONAL taxonomy -- (A) Evaluation Objectives (WHAT to evaluate): Agent Behavior (task completion, output quality, latency&cost), Agent Capabilities (tool use, planning&reasoning, memory&context retention, multi-agent collaboration), Reliability (consistency, robustness), Safety & Alignment (fairness, harm/toxicity/bias, compliance&privacy); and (B) Evaluation Process (HOW to evaluate): Interaction Mode (static&offline vs dynamic&online), Evaluation Data (synthetic/real-world datasets, domain benchmarks), Metrics Computation Methods (code-based, LLM-as-a-Judge / Agent-as-a-Judge, human-in-the-loop), Evaluation Tooling (LangSmith, Arize/Phoenix, DeepEval, InspectAI, GALILEO, OpenAI Evals, Azure AI Foundry, Google Vertex AI, LangGraph, Amazon Bedrock; leaderboards: BFCL, Holistic Agent Leaderboard), Evaluation Contexts. Plus enterprise-specific challenges and future directions. Coverage window: through ~2025 (v1 submitted Jul 2025). Reference count: approximately 128 references (max in-text bib index 128).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (this is a survey, not a benchmark; it constructs no dataset and reports no dataset size or best-system score of its own). It does survey benchmark CONSTRUCTION practices (human-annotated, synthetic, and interaction-generated data; gold tool sequences with expected parameter structures; execution-based verification a la Gorilla).
builds_on: Builds on prior LLM-evaluation methodology (LLM-as-a-Judge, Zheng et al. 2023) extended to agents (Agent-as-a-Judge, Zhuge et al. 2024), and synthesizes agent-capability and benchmark literature: ReAct (Yao et al. 2023), tool-use/function-calling benchmarks (Gorilla/Patil 2023, API-Bank/Li 2023, ToolBench, TaskBench/Shen 2024, T-Eval/Chen 2024b, BFCL/Yan 2024), planning benchmarks (AgentBoard/Ma 2024, ScienceAgentBench/Chen 2025), memory benchmarks (LongEval, SocialBench, LoCoMo/Maharana 2024, Optimus-1/Li 2024d), web/app benchmarks (WebArena/Zhou 2023, AppWorld/Trivedi 2024, AssistantBench/Yoran 2024), and safety benchmarks (AgentHarm/Andriushchenko 2025, AgentDojo/Debenedetti 2024). Aggregates rather than extends a single predecessor.
contrasts_with: Positions itself against the fragmented, capability-narrow prior evaluation landscape that lacks a unifying framework, and against research that overlooks enterprise deployment concerns (role-based data access, reliability guarantees, dynamic/long-horizon interaction, compliance). As a survey it complements and is distinct from other contemporaneous agent-evaluation surveys, notably Yehudai et al. 'Survey on Evaluation of LLM-based Agents' (arXiv:2503.16416) -- which the task brief appears to have conflated with this paper -- by emphasizing the WHAT/HOW (objectives/process) two-axis taxonomy and enterprise challenges.
lineage: Surveys group: a 2025 survey specializing in EVALUATION & BENCHMARKING of LLM agents (WHAT/HOW two-dimensional taxonomy with enterprise focus). It is an umbrella reference for the evaluation/benchmark sub-topics that the retrieval-augmented-agent lineage relies on -- in particular it catalogs the memory benchmarks (LoCoMo, SocialBench, LongEval, Optimus-1) and tool-use benchmarks (ToolBench, API-Bank, TaskBench, T-Eval, BFCL) used to evaluate the memory/tool-retrieval methods in Groups A-F -- rather than being a method within any single sub-topic.
